text: Every month the variable rate sits below nine percent, Leah pays less interest than on the fixed loan, and that saving builds a cushion. The cushion grows fastest at the start, when she owes the most, so every point of rate is charged on the biggest balance. When the rate later climbs above nine percent, the extra interest has to use up that cushion before the variable loan has cost more overall. A short jump above nine percent only dents it; emptying it needs rates that rise early and stay high for years. In a stretch where rates drift down, the cushion just keeps growing.
